title: A thirty-dollar delivery trip to Philadelphia
summary: A story of a hauling job for a neighbor that netted him almost nothing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. Oh, that's way late. That's round about before we got married...no, after we got married...
Well, '28 was way before you got married.
Yeah, I know. Well, this is after we got married. It must have been about '50, '55, '60, somewhere around in there...

But anyway, I lived at 115 West 141st Street, on the fourth floor. And I got a chance to make some extra money, to go... I went to see a friend of mine. Some lady across the street from where I lived, she asked me did I

want to make thirty dollars. Thirty dollars. Thirty dollars then... I wasn't thinking about all the tolls that had to come out that. I had about five or six tolls that come out of that thirty dollars. I had to buy gas, you know. So I didn't want to go by myself, so I got my brother-in-law to go with me. And the stuff weighed around about...it was almost 500 pounds. There was a lot of cut glass and silver, knives and forks. She said to give it to somebody in Philadelphia. So I ended up coming back, I didn't have nothin'. All the money I had was twelve dollars.
